metaTitle: Product Design for AI Startups & AI SaaS | Designit
metaDescription: Product and UX design for AI startups, AI SaaS and agentic products: interfaces, workflows and strategy for software whose output isn't fully predictable.
h1: Product design for AI startups and AI-native software
subtitle: AI products fail less often on model quality than on product design: people don't know what to ask, can't tell when to trust the answer, and can't follow what an agent did. We design the product around the model so it gets used, and used safely.
author: Designit

sections.heading: Our point of view
paras: Design the wrong answer first. If an AI feature cannot gracefully handle a confident mistake, it is not ready, however good the model is.
Match autonomy to reversibility. Suggest when mistakes are cheap, draft when people will check the work, and require approval before anything that can't be undone.
Show the basis, not a disclaimer. Sources and the data an answer used build calibrated trust; generic warnings teach people to ignore warnings.

faq.q: What do AI startups most often get wrong in product design?
faq.a: Shipping a blank prompt box instead of guiding a task, designing only the happy path, and giving no way to see or correct what the AI did. Those choices make strong models feel unreliable.

faq.q: How should an AI SaaS product onboard new users?
faq.a: With example tasks rather than an empty prompt, honest limits up front, and a first success in the first session that shows what the product is for.

faq.q: Can you show us AI work you've done?
faq.a: Much of it is under NDA, so we walk through relevant work on a call rather than publishing it.
